title: Victor's studio and the Frederick Brothers booking agency
summary: Victor was near 45th and 6th; Frederick Brothers booked Oliver and had him record before touring; Moore had his own agent for his trio.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Where were the Victor Studios? I know they were in New York, but what streets were they on?
I think it was on 45th Street, a place there in some studio... 45th Street and 6th Avenue.
Do you remember who was in charge of the sessions at Victor? Those King Oliver sessions, who actually produced the recordings?
Well, we went through our booking agent, who was Frederick Brothers.
They used to book Oliver on those gigs...

Yeah, on down to Kansas City, all down through there -- the Frederick Brothers. And he saw that... Of course, they were making some money on the band. Well, he wanted to record the band first before he went on the road. And they found the Victor Company... They wanted to have some big sounds. And most of them come out pretty good.
When you had your own trio, did you have a booking agent or a manager or someone...??
No. I had my own booking agent.
